results.title: Parts and Accessories Necessary for Safe Operation; Certification and Labeling Requirements for Rear Impact Protection Guards

statements.text: FMCSA proposes to amend the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations to rescind the requirement that rear impact guards be permanently marked or labeled with a certification from the impact guard manufacturer as required by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard.

FMCSA proposes to amend the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSRs) to rescind the requirement that the rear impact guard be permanently marked or labeled with a certification from the impact guard manufacturer as required by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's (NHTSA) applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS).

The certification label or marking currently provides motor carriers purchasing new trailers or replacement impact guards with a means to determine whether the equipment is certified as meeting the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard.
The labeling or marking requirement has proven problematic when the label or marking becomes illegible or wears off during the service life of the trailer or guard.

The proposal would eliminate an unintended regulatory burden on motor carriers without compromising safety, as this notice of proposed rulemaking would not affect the applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard.
The final rule eliminates an unintended regulatory burden on motor carriers without compromising safety, as it does not affect the applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard.
